source.title: Extracting Possibly Representative COVID-19 Biomarkers from X-ray Images with Deep Learning Approach and Image Data Related to Pulmonary Diseases
source.authors: Ioannis D. Apostolopoulos; Sokratis I. Aznaouridis; Mpesiana A. Tzani

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. In the training-from-scratch results, Table 5 reports 7-class accuracy as 87.66%, while the accompanying prose says 86.66%.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains MobileNet v2 from scratch on pulmonary X-ray images and reports classification results, extending the training-from-scratch setting to a different task. It does not report training classification error, so it does not directly test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out cross-validation accuracy and related metrics, not training error. Those results do not establish whether the network reached zero or near-zero training error. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses CNN training and batch normalization for pulmonary X-ray classification, reporting only held-out classification performance. It measures neither training error nor the optimization comparisons named in V1–V6. Section 2.3.1 cites Santurkar et al. for batch normalization but provides no normalization ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report that training from scratch performed best among their tested strategies and suggest investigating whether its extracted features constitute biomarkers. Their conclusion also emphasizes automatic COVID-19 detection and its potential to reduce staff exposure; biomarker validity was proposed for future research rather than established.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains MobileNet v2 from scratch on pulmonary X-rays and reports cross-validation classification metrics; the listed versions concern other tasks and training-error, optimization, depth, initialization, and normalization outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Classification metrics differ across the tested feature-learning strategies and fine-tuning settings; the paper does not report corresponding training-error values.

fits_no_version.finding: Training MobileNet v2 from scratch achieved 99.18% held-out 2-class accuracy and 87.66% held-out 7-class accuracy in Table 5, exceeding the tested transfer-learning strategies. The accompanying prose instead gives 86.66% for 7-class accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training MobileNet v2 from scratch outperforms the tested frozen-feature and fine-tuning strategies on this pulmonary X-ray dataset under 10-fold cross-validation.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Medical and Biological Engineering
record.problems: The paper reports evaluation metrics rather than training error, so its results do not show whether the network fit the training data. The 7-class accuracy is inconsistent between Table 5 and the accompanying prose. Dataset limitations include a relatively small COVID-19 sample and possible labeling errors in the NIH data.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports results for off-the-shelf features and six fine-tuning settings in Tables 1 and 4. These are evaluation metrics for transfer-learning strategies, not training-error results bearing on the listed versions, so they are not extracted.

untested.parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/100, corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size, early stopping or regularization on fitting.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons and training very deep networks without shortcuts or normalization.
Effects of initialization on training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics and divergence.
Effects of batch normalization on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the reader's tests/T3 classification to uses_without_test/T4. A new application with held-out accuracy alone does not test these optimization claims. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, training classification error, or the effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization on training error.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or spurious-local-minimum analysis.
No comparison of plain and residual networks or depth effects on training error.
No comparison of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability or sharpness analysis.
No comparison of batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: Mobile Net v2
rows.operation_detail: Training from scratch with 10-fold cross-validation on the pulmonary X-ray dataset; reported metrics are evaluation results, not training error.
rows.note: Held-out classification accuracy does not show whether training classification error was zero or near zero.
rows.check: The 99.18% value is mean held-out 2-class accuracy under 10-fold cross-validation, not training accuracy. It cannot establish any listed optimization effect.

rows.subject: Mobile Net v2
